Data source overview:
This paper introduces “Trust Score”, a post-hoc metric that compares a test point’s distance to the core of the predicted class against its distance to the nearest alternative class.  It includes:  (1) an α-high-density-set estimator (Algorithm 1);  (2) the Trust-Score computation (Algorithm 2);  (3) theoretical guarantees relating the score to Bayes-optimal agreement; and (4) empirical studies that show substantial gains in low-dimensional settings and show how to regain usefulness in high-dimensional tasks through latent representations.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]
Instruction set could be improved by: a) explicitly clarifying allowable edge direction semantics for “implemented_by/refined_by” to avoid ambiguity; b) adding an example with multiple interventions refined from one parent to illustrate legal outgoing edges from interventions; c) specifying whether concept→concept edges may have multiple verbs simultaneously when two relations hold.

Inference strategy justification:
Nearly all nodes and edges are drawn directly from text.  Light inference (confidence 2 edges) was used only for scalability refinement (“skip filtering”) and for mapping empirical limitations to efficiency-oriented interventions, as the authors mention them informally.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All major reasoning elements linking the primary risk (unreliable confidences) through methodological steps (density filtering, trust score), theoretical/empirical support, to four concrete interventions are captured.  Every node participates in at least one edge, and multiple paths interconnect through shared nodes, forming a single fabric.

Key limitations:
1. The paper is confined to supervised classification; therefore higher-level AI-safety risks like deceptive alignment are outside scope.  
2. Effectiveness of interventions relies on domain-specific hyper-parameters which are not fully formalised in the graph.  
3. Empirical evidence is limited to moderate-scale datasets, so maturity assignments remain at level 2.
